message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Atomic Data** | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | H‑1 (protium), H‑2 (deuterium), H‑3 (tritium) |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV (first) |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV |
| **Physical State at STP** | Phase | Gas |
| | Boiling point | –252.9 °C (20.3 K) |
| | Melting point | –259.2 °C (14.0 K) |
| | Density (gas) | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ |
| | Molar volume | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Specific heat (gas, 25 °C) | 28.8 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Heat of vaporization | 0.449 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Speed of sound | ~ 1275 m s⁻¹ (at 20 °C) |
| **Chemical Behavior** | Bond type | Covalent (H₂) |
| | Bond dissociation energy | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Oxidation state | +1 (in acids, salts) |
| | Redox potential (vs SHE) | 0 V (standard hydrogen electrode) |
| | Reactivity | Highly reactive with halogens, metals, and nonmetals; forms hydrides (e.g., NaH, CaH₂). |
| | Combustion | 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (exothermic, ΔH ≈ –286 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Solubility in water | 0.0006 g g⁻¹ (≈ 0.6 mg mL⁻¹) |
| | Solubility in organic solvents | Variable; high in supercritical CO₂ |
| **Isotopic Variants** | Protium (¹H) | Stable, most abundant |
| | Deuterium (²H) | Stable, 0.015% natural abundance |
| | Tritium (³H) | Radioactive (half‑life 12.32 y), used in nuclear fusion research |
| **Spectroscopic Features** | Rotational spectrum | Microwave region (e.g., 1420 MHz hyperfine transition of neutral hydrogen) |
| | Vibrational frequency (H₂) | 4401 cm⁻¹ |
| | Electronic transitions | UV–visible absorption (e.g., Lyman series) |
| **Applications & Roles** | Energy carrier | Hydrogen fuel cells, rocket propellant |
| | Chemical feedstock | Production of ammonia (NH₃), methanol (CH₃OH), and other organics |
| | Nuclear fusion | Deuterium–tritium fusion (D-T) reaction |
| | Astrophysics | Most abundant element in the universe; key in stellar nucleosynthesis |
| | Analytical chemistry | Used as a standard in mass spectrometry (H₂⁺, H₃⁺ ions) |
| | Medical imaging | Hyperpolarized ^13C‑labeled deuterated compounds for MRI contrast |
| **Safety & Handling** | Flammability | Extremely flammable; explosive limits 4–75 % (v/v) in air |
| | Toxicity | Non‑toxic, but can cause asphyxiation in confined spaces |
| | Storage | Requires high‑pressure cylinders or cryogenic tanks; careful leak detection |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Hydrogen is the simplest element**: one proton, one electron, no neutrons in its most common isotope (protium).
- **It exists mainly as diatomic gas (H₂)** under normal conditions, but can form a wide variety of compounds (hydrides, acids, organics).
- **Its isotopes have distinct nuclear properties**: deuterium is stable and useful in NMR; tritium is radioactive and central to fusion research.
- **Hydrogen’s low density and high reactivity** make it ideal as an energy carrier (fuel cells, rockets) but also require stringent safety protocols.
- **In the cosmos, hydrogen fuels stars** via nuclear fusion, producing heavier elements and releasing energy that sustains life on Earth.

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property or application!
